mainTopic: Honoring the dead, the שכינה in exile, the holiness of בתי כנסיות and בתי קברות, and the four special שבת readings
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא: we stop תלמוד תורה to escort the dead and to bring a bride to her wedding, but only when there are not already enough people. רב, עולא, and רב ששת each define 'enough' differently, and for a scholar who taught others there is no limit at all. Next, רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that the שכינה went with ישראל into every exile and will return with them. אביי names the synagogues in בבל where the שכינה rests, and two stories show the שכינה coming there. Several sages read פסוקים to show that בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות are a 'מקדש מעט', and רבי אלעזר הקפר says they will one day be moved to ארץ ישראל. בר קפרא teaches that the mountains that competed with סיני were 'blemished', and רב אשי learns that an arrogant person is a בעל מום. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's rules about a ruined בית כנסת: the shortcut ban and its exceptions, and the grass growing inside it. It also brings parallel rules about respecting a בית הקברות. Finally, a new משנה lists the four special שבתות readings and the other days that interrupt the regular order. The גמרא begins discussing it by quoting the משנה about the שקלים announcement, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: We stop Torah learning for a funeral or a wedding
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one stops תלמוד תורה to escort the dead and to escort a bride.
steps.simpleTranslation: We interrupt Torah learning in order to carry out the dead for burial and to bring a bride to her wedding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a basic rule: some מצוות are important enough that we stop learning Torah for them. The two examples are a funeral and a wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally תלמוד תורה is the highest מצוה, and we do not stop learning for most things. Here the ברייתא says two acts of kindness, honoring the dead and making a bride happy, do override learning. Later steps will limit this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying out the dead for burial (a funeral)
Bringing the bride in (escorting her to her wedding)

phrases.english: We interrupt Torah study
to carry out the dead for burial,
and to escort a bride to her wedding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the topic here.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah learning is interrupted for a funeral and for escorting a bride.

steps.title: רבי יהודה ברבי אילעאי actually did this
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reports that רבי יהודה ברבי אילעאי stopped learning for funerals and weddings.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי יהודה son of רבי אילעאי that he used to stop his Torah learning to escort the dead and to escort a bride.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows a real-life example: a great תנא actually lived by this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new law. It is a story that backs up the rule from step 1. It shows that even a great scholar, whose learning is very valuable, stopped for these מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: They said about him (introduces a report about a sage's conduct)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִילְעַאי
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Elai,
that he would interrupt his Torah study
to carry out the dead and to escort a bride.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִילְעַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule of step 1 with the conduct of a sage.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that Torah study is interrupted for a funeral and a bride.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבי יהודה ברבי אילעאי.

steps.title: Only when there are not enough people already
steps.stepSummary: The rule is limited: we stop learning only if there are not already enough people present.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? When there are not enough people there. But if there are already enough people there, we do not stop learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the rule from step 1. You only have to stop learning if the funeral or wedding does not already have enough people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'במה דברים אמורים' always narrows an earlier rule. Here the point is that the goal is proper honor for the dead or the bride. Once that honor is fully given, extra people should keep learning. This raises the obvious next question: how many people count as 'enough'?

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (introduces a limitation)
All that is needed (a full, proper number of people)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the rule. It only says the rule applies when more people are actually needed.

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
When there are not enough people there,
but if there are enough people there,
we do not interrupt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of step 1 to cases where more people are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning is interrupted only when the funeral or wedding does not already have a full number of people.

steps.title: How many people count as enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what number counts as כל צורכו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many people is 'enough'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question about step 3. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 used the term כל צורכו but did not give a number. Without a number, nobody knows when he may keep learning. The next steps give several opinions.

phrases.english: And how many is 'enough'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure behind the limitation in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The number of people that counts as כל צורכו.

steps.title: רב's answer: twelve thousand men and six thousand horns
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר איניא in the name of רב says twelve thousand men plus six thousand horn-blowers; a second version says the six thousand are included in the twelve thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר איניא said in the name of רב: twelve thousand men, and six thousand horns. Some say it this way: twelve thousand men, and among them six thousand horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer: a very large number of people. There are two versions of how to count it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version there are 18,000 people: 12,000 men plus 6,000 more blowing שופרות. In the second version there are only 12,000 total, and 6,000 of them are the horn-blowers. Either way, 'enough' is a huge crowd.

keyTerms.meaning: Horns (blown as a sign of mourning)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Inya said in the name of Rav:
Twelve thousand men,
and six thousand horns.
And some say:
Twelve thousand men,
and among them six thousand with horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Twelve thousand men with six thousand horns, either in addition or included.

steps.title: עולא's answer: a line from the city gate to the burial place
steps.stepSummary: עולא says 'enough' means enough people to form a line from the city gate to the burial place.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: for example, enough men to form a line from the city gate all the way to the burial place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. עולא does not give a fixed number. He measures by the distance of the procession.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עולא, 'enough' depends on the place. If the people fill the whole path from the city gate to the burial place, the honor is complete. This is a different kind of measure than רב's fixed number.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
For example, enough men to form a line
from the city gate to the burial place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 4, different from רב's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Enough people to fill the route from the city gate to the burial place.

steps.title: רב ששת: as the Torah was given, so it is taken
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the funeral of a Torah scholar needs six hundred thousand people, just like at מתן תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: as the Torah was given, so it is taken away. Just as it was given in front of six hundred thousand, so too its taking away should be in front of six hundred thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. רב ששת compares the death of a Torah scholar to the day the Torah was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a Torah scholar dies, the Torah inside him is 'taken away' from the world. So his funeral should have the same crowd as מתן תורה at Sinai: 600,000, the number of men in ישראל then. This is a much bigger number than the earlier answers.

keyTerms.meaning: As its giving, so is its taking

steps.confusionAlert: 'Its taking' does not mean the Torah is forgotten. It means the death of a scholar who carried the Torah.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
As the Torah was given, so is it taken away.
Just as it was given in the presence of six hundred thousand,
so too its taking is in the presence of six hundred thousand.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: כִּנְתִינָתָהּ כָּךְ נְטִילָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 4, based on a comparison to מתן תורה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Six hundred thousand people, like at מתן תורה.

steps.title: For one who taught others, there is no limit
steps.stepSummary: The 600,000 measure is for a scholar who only learned himself; for one who taught others, there is no upper limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies to someone who read and learned for himself. But for someone who taught others, there is no limit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב ששת's number. It applies only to a scholar who learned for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who taught Torah to others spread Torah further. So no number of people is ever 'enough' for his funeral, and everyone should stop learning to come. This ends the discussion of how many people are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Who read Scripture and learned משנה (for himself)
There is no measure / limit for him

steps.whatToRemember: We stop learning for a funeral or a wedding only if more people are needed. רב, עולא, and רב ששת disagree on what 'enough' is. For a scholar who taught others, there is no limit at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the honor given at a funeral matches the Torah the person gave to the world, and teaching others counts most.

phrases.english: This applies to someone who read and studied for himself,
but for someone who taught others,
there is no limit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב ששת's 600,000 to a scholar who did not teach others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a scholar who taught others, there is no upper limit to the people needed at his funeral.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: the שכינה goes with ישראל into every exile
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא opens: ישראל are so beloved that the שכינה went with them wherever they were exiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: Come and see how beloved ישראל are before הקב"ה, for in every place they were exiled, the שכינה was with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן יוחי makes a general claim, and the next steps will prove it from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that God did not leave ישראל when they went into exile. Instead, the שכינה went into exile with them. This shows how much He loves them.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:
Come and see how beloved the Jewish people are
before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
for in every place they were exiled,
the Divine Presence was with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new, unrelated אגדה ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה accompanies ישראל into every exile.

steps.title: Proof from the exile in Egypt
steps.stepSummary: The שכינה was with ישראל in מצרים, as a פסוק in שמואל shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were exiled to Egypt, and the שכינה was with them, as it says: 'I revealed Myself to your father's house when they were in Egypt.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי proves his claim with the first example: the exile in מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says God revealed Himself to ישראל while they were in Egypt. That means His presence was there with them during the exile.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: They were exiled to Egypt, and the Divine Presence was with them,
as it is stated: 'Did I reveal Myself to the house of your father
when they were in Egypt, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First proof for the claim in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The שכינה went with ישראל into exile.

steps.title: Proof from the exile in Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: The שכינה was with ישראל in בבל, as a פסוק in ישעיהו shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were exiled to Babylonia, and the שכינה was with them, as it says: 'For your sake I was sent to Babylonia.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second example: the exile to בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God says 'I was sent to Babylonia for your sake,' meaning He Himself went there with ישראל. This shows the pattern repeats in a second exile.

phrases.english: They were exiled to Babylonia, and the Divine Presence was with them,
as it is stated: 'For your sake I was sent to Babylonia.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second proof for the claim in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The שכינה went with ישראל into exile.

steps.title: In the future redemption, God will return with them
steps.stepSummary: At the future גאולה, the שכינה will return together with ישראל, learned from the word 'ושב' instead of 'והשיב.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And also when they will be redeemed in the future, the שכינה will be with them, as it says: 'And ה׳ your God will return with your captivity.' It does not say 'He will bring back,' but 'He will return.' This teaches that הקב"ה returns with them from among the exiles.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי gives the last example: the future גאולה. He reads one word in the פסוק very carefully to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק said 'והשיב,' it would mean God brings ישראל back while He stays where He is. It says 'ושב,' 'He will return,' which means God Himself is coming back too. So the שכינה is in exile with ישראל and will come home with them.

keyTerms.meaning: Will be redeemed in the future
And He will return (God Himself returns)
And He will bring back (God returns others)

steps.whatToRemember: The שכינה went with ישראל to מצרים and to בבל, and it will return with them at the גאולה. The proof is that the פסוק says 'ושב,' 'He returns,' and not 'והשיב,' 'He brings back.'
steps.confusionAlert: The proof depends on the grammar: 'ושב' means God Himself returns, while 'והשיב' would mean He only brings others back.

phrases.english: And also, when in the future they will be redeemed,
the Divine Presence will be with them,
as it is stated: 'And the Lord your God will return with your captivity.'
It does not say 'He will bring back,' but rather 'He will return.'
This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
returns with them from among the exiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף כְּשֶׁהֵן עֲתִידִין לִיגָּאֵל — שְׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final proof, extending the claim of step 9 to the future גאולה.
steps.raayaObject: The שכינה is with ישראל in exile and will return with them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים ל:ג, read precisely: 'ושב' rather than 'והשיב.'

steps.title: Where in Babylonia does the Divine Presence rest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the specific place in בבל where the שכינה rests.
steps.simpleTranslation: In בבל, where is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא said the שכינה is with ישראל in בבל. Now the גמרא asks exactly where in בבל, setting up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא made a general statement about the whole exile. This question asks for a concrete, physical location.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylonia, the main land of exile

phrases.english: In Babylonia, where?
phrases.notes: Refers back to the ברייתא in Step 11

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact location behind the general claim in Step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific place in בבל where the שכינה rests

steps.title: Two synagogues, the Divine Presence alternating between them
steps.stepSummary: אביי names the בית כנסת of הוצל and the בית כנסת of שף ויתיב in נהרדעא. The שכינה goes back and forth between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In the בית כנסת of הוצל, and in the בית כנסת of "שף ויתיב" in נהרדעא. Do not say it is in both places at the same time. Rather, sometimes it is here and sometimes there.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by naming two specific synagogues. He then makes clear that the שכינה is in one of them at a time, not in both at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer names two places. That raises the question of whether the שכינה is in both at the same moment. אביי heads this off: it moves between them at different times.

keyTerms.meaning: A town in בבל with an ancient synagogue
"Slipped and settled". Name of a famous synagogue in נהרדעא
A major Jewish city in בבל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read "here and here" as the שכינה being in both places at once. The גמרא says outright that it alternates.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In the synagogue of Huzal,
and in the synagogue of "Shaf VeYativ" in Neharde'a.
phrases.notes: According to tradition, this synagogue was built with stones and earth brought from ירושלים

phrases.english: And do not say: here and here (at once),
rather, sometimes here and sometimes here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שכינה rests in the synagogues of הוצל and שף ויתיב, alternating between them

steps.title: אביי's practice of praying in these synagogues
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he deserves reward because whenever he is within a פרסה of these synagogues, he goes in to pray there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Let a blessing come to me, for when I am a פרסה away, I go in and pray there.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי describes his own practice. Because the שכינה rests in these synagogues, he makes the effort to pray there whenever he is close enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the information from Step 14 into practice. Knowing where the שכינה rests leads him to go out of his way to pray in those places.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let it come to me". I deserve a reward
Parasang, a distance of about 4 מיל

phrases.english: Abaye said: (A blessing) should come to me,
for when I am (only) a parasang away,
I go in and pray there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical consequence from Step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is worthwhile to go out of one's way to pray where the שכינה rests

steps.title: שמואל's father and Levi leave when the Divine Presence comes
steps.stepSummary: While אבוה דשמואל and לוי sat in the שף ויתיב synagogue, the שכינה came. They heard a loud noise, got up, and left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of שמואל and לוי were sitting in the synagogue of שף ויתיב in נהרדעא. The שכינה came, they heard a loud noise, and they got up and left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the שכינה really did come to the שף ויתיב synagogue. The two sages left out of respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story backs up אביי's claim with an event that actually happened. It also teaches the proper reaction: making room for the שכינה by leaving.

keyTerms.meaning: The father of שמואל (named אבא בר אבא)

phrases.english: The father of Shmuel and Levi

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ יָתְבִי בִּכְנִישְׁתָּא דְּשַׁף וִיתֵיב בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא.
phrases.english: were sitting in the synagogue of Shaf VeYativ in Neharde'a.
The Divine Presence came,
they heard a loud noise,
they got up and left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 14 with a story
steps.raayaObject: That the שכינה rests in the שף ויתיב synagogue
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident with אבוה דשמואל and לוי

steps.title: רב ששת stays, and is allowed to remain
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת did not leave when the שכינה came. The angels frightened him, he argued that the afflicted one should not have to give way, and הקב"ה told the angels to leave him alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת was sitting in the synagogue of שף ויתיב in נהרדעא. The שכינה came and he did not leave. The מלאכי השרת came and frightened him. He said before Him: Master of the World, when one is afflicted and one is not, who should give way to whom? He (הקב"ה) said to them: Leave him.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story about the same synagogue. רב ששת, who was blind, stayed put. When the angels tried to scare him away, he pleaded with הקב"ה and was allowed to stay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story also confirms that the שכינה came there. רב ששת's argument is that the one who is suffering (he was blind) should not have to step aside for those who are not suffering (the angels). הקב"ה agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives way to, is pushed aside for

steps.confusionAlert: "Afflicted" refers to רב ששת himself (he was blind), and "not afflicted" refers to the angels. He is asking why he should have to give way to them.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet was sitting
in the synagogue of Shaf VeYativ in Neharde'a,
the Divine Presence came and he did not leave.
The ministering angels came
and were frightening him.
He said before Him: Master of the World,
(one who is) afflicted and (one who is) not afflicted,
who gives way before whom?
He said to them: Leave him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא דְּשַׁף וִיתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about the same synagogue, with a different outcome
steps.raayaObject: That the שכינה rests in the שף ויתיב synagogue

steps.title: "A small sanctuary" means the synagogues and study halls of Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads the פסוק "ואהי להם למקדש מעט" as referring to the בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And I became for them a small מקדש." רבי יצחק said: These are the synagogues and study halls in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from יחזקאל about הקב"ה being a "small מקדש" for ישראל in exile. רבי יצחק says this means the synagogues and study halls of בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a scriptural basis for the holiness of these places. In exile, the בית כנסת and בית מדרש act as a miniature בית המקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that the בית כנסת is a "מקדש מעט", is the source of much of the honor and respect we give synagogues in הלכה.

phrases.english: "And I became for them a small sanctuary" (Ezekiel 11:16),
Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת שֶׁבְּבָבֶל.
phrases.english: These are the synagogues and study halls in Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: וָאֱהִי לָהֶם לְמִקְדָּשׁ מְעַט, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stories about specific synagogues to a פסוק about synagogues in general
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות of בבל are the "מקדש מעט"

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the house of our master in Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads "מקדש מעט" as referring to the בית רבינו in בבל, the study hall of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: This is the house of our master in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר offers a different reading of the same פסוק. He applies it to one specific place: the בית מדרש of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק applied the פסוק to all the synagogues and study halls. רבי אלעזר narrows it to the great yeshiva of רב, from which Torah spread to the whole world.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of our master, the בית מדרש of רב

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
This is the house of our master in Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: זֶה בֵּית רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁבְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion on the same פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "מקדש מעט" refers specifically to רב's study hall in בבל

steps.title: "You have been our dwelling place" means synagogues and study halls
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains "ה׳ מעון אתה היית לנו" as referring to בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does it mean when it says, "ה׳, You have been a dwelling place for us"? These are the synagogues and study halls.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings another פסוק, from תהלים, and reads the word "מעון" (dwelling place) as referring to synagogues and study halls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a second פסוק supporting the same idea. The places where Jews pray and learn are where הקב"ה "dwells" with them in every generation.

phrases.english: Rava expounded: What is that which is written:
"Lord, You have been a dwelling place for us" (Psalms 90:1),
these are the synagogues and study halls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק supporting the theme of Step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "מעון" refers to בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות

steps.title: אביי moves his Torah learning into the synagogue
steps.stepSummary: אביי used to learn at home and pray in the בית כנסת. After hearing דוד's words "ה׳ אהבתי מעון ביתך", he began learning in the בית כנסת too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: At first I used to learn at home and pray in the בית כנסת. Once I heard what דוד said, "ה׳, I love the dwelling place of Your house," I began learning in the בית כנסת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes the section with his personal practice. Because of a פסוק about loving הקב"ה's house, he moved his learning into the synagogue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building on the idea that the synagogue is הקב"ה's "dwelling place", אביי understood that spending more time there shows love for it. So he moved his learning there as well, not only his davening.

keyTerms.meaning: The dwelling place of Your house

steps.whatToRemember: The שכינה rests in specific synagogues in בבל, and בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות in general are a "מקדש מעט" and הקב"ה's "מעון". That is why אביי prayed, and later also learned, in the בית כנסת.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
At first I used to learn at home
and pray in the synagogue,
once I heard that which David says:
"Lord, I love the dwelling place of Your house" (Psalms 26:8),
I would learn in the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוַאי גָּרֵיסְנָא בְּבֵיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the theme of Steps 18 and 20 in personal practice
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Out of love for הקב"ה's dwelling place, one should also learn Torah in the בית כנסת

steps.title: The synagogues of Babylonia will be moved to the Land of Israel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אלעזר הקפר: in the future, the בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות of בבל will be set up in ארץ ישראל, based on a פסוק about תבור and כרמל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי אלעזר הקפר says: In the future, the synagogues and study halls of בבל will be set up in ארץ ישראל, as it says: 'Like תבור among the mountains, and like כרמל by the sea, so shall he come.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that continues the praise of בתי כנסיות. It says that the synagogues of בבל will one day be moved to ארץ ישראל, and it quotes a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps showed that the שכינה is found in the בתי כנסיות of בבל. This ברייתא goes further: these buildings are so holy that they will be moved to ארץ ישראל in the future. The פסוק about תבור and כרמל is the base for the קל וחומר in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: That they will be set up permanently
Two mountains, Mount Tabor and Mount Carmel

steps.confusionAlert: Background you need: there is a tradition that תבור and כרמל came to מתן תורה hoping the Torah would be given on them. The פסוק 'so shall he come' is read as describing that trip, and it implies they were then set down in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar says:

phrases.aramaic: עֲתִידִין בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת שֶׁבְּבָבֶל
phrases.english: In the future, the synagogues and study halls in Babylonia
will be set up in the Land of Israel,
as it says: 'Surely, like Tabor among the mountains,
and like Carmel by the sea, so shall he come.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the praise of the בתי כנסיות of בבל from the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות of בבל will in the future be set up in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Proving it with a קל וחומר from תבור and כרמל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains with a קל וחומר: if תבור and כרמל, which came only briefly for Torah, earned a place in ארץ ישראל, then buildings where Torah is always read and taught surely will.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? If תבור and כרמל, which came only for a short time to learn Torah, are set up in ארץ ישראל, then synagogues and study halls, where Torah is read and taught, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows exactly how the פסוק proves its point. It uses a קל וחומר, a 'how much more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'lighter' case is תבור and כרמל, which came to Torah only once, for a short moment, and still got a place in ארץ ישראל as a reward. The 'heavier' case is the בתי כנסיות, where Torah is read and spread all the time. So they deserve the same reward even more.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a heavier case: 'how much more so'

phrases.english: And isn't this a kal vachomer:
If Tabor and Carmel,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בָּאוּ אֶלָּא לְפִי שָׁעָה לִלְמוֹד תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: which came only for a moment to learn Torah,
are set up in the Land of Israel,
then synagogues and study halls
in which Torah is read and spread —
all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 22 proves the claim.
steps.raayaObject: That the בתי כנסיות of בבל will be moved to ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from תבור and כרמל, which came briefly to Torah and were set up in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: A Heavenly Voice tells the mountains they cannot compete with Sinai
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא explains the פסוק 'למה תרצדון הרים גבנונים': a בת קול told the mountains not to argue with סיני, because they are all 'blemished' next to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: What does it mean, 'Why do you look jealously, you peaked mountains'? A בת קול came out and said to them: Why do you want to argue a case against סיני? All of you are blemished compared to סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: Staying with the mountains theme, בר קפרא reads a פסוק in תהלים as a scene at מתן תורה. The mountains wanted the Torah, and a בת קול told them they had no case against סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word תרצדון as a wordplay: תרצו דין, 'you want a court case'. The mountains were asking to be chosen instead of סיני. The answer is that they are all 'blemished', and the next step proves where that word comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained a פסוק in a deeper, non-literal way
You look jealously; read here as תִּרְצוּ דִּין, 'you want a court case'
Ones with a blemish or physical defect

phrases.english: Bar Kappara taught:
What is meant by what is written: 'Why do you look jealously, you peaked mountains'?
A Heavenly Voice went out and said to them:
Why do you want a court case against Sinai?
phrases.notes: This is a play on the word תרצדון from the פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלְּכֶם בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִים אַתֶּם אֵצֶל סִינַי.
phrases.english: All of you are blemished compared to Sinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the theme of mountains at מתן תורה from the previous ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The other mountains had no claim against סיני, because compared to it they were 'blemished'.

steps.title: Why 'peaked' means 'blemished'
steps.stepSummary: A word link: גבנונים here is like גבן, one of the blemishes that disqualifies a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here 'peaked (גבנונים)', and it is written there, about a כהן's blemishes: 'or a hunchback (גבן) or a dwarf.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the source for calling the mountains 'blemished'. It links the word גבנונים to the word גבן, a hunchback, which is a מום for a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא, a hunchbacked כהן cannot do the עבודה because it is a מום. Since the mountains are called by a similar word, they too are considered 'blemished'. This sets up the lesson רב אשי takes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there (a word link between two פסוקים)
Hunchback, a blemish that disqualifies a כהן

phrases.english: It is written here: 'peaked',
and it is written there: 'or a hunchback or a dwarf.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כא:כ, the blemishes of a כהן

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the word 'blemished' used in step 24.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The link between גבנונים in תהלים and גבן in the list of a כהן's blemishes.

steps.title: An arrogant person is considered blemished
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי learns from this: a person who is arrogant counts as a בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Learn from this that someone who is arrogant is a blemished person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי draws a moral lesson from בר קפרא's teaching. Since the mountains pushed themselves forward and were called blemished, an arrogant person is also blemished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mountains' flaw was not their shape. It was that they proudly demanded the Torah for themselves. רב אשי turns this into a general rule about people: arrogance is a real defect, like a physical מום.
steps.whatToRemember: The other mountains arrogantly demanded the Torah and were called 'blemished' next to סיני. From this רב אשי learns that an arrogant person is a בעל מום.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Learn from this

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דִּיהִיר — בַּעַל מוּם הוּא.
phrases.english: that one who is arrogant is a blemished person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical lesson from בר קפרא's teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An arrogant person is considered a בעל מום.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: what is a קפנדריא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a בית כנסת may not be used as a קפנדריא, and asks what that word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'We may not make it a קפנדריא.' What is a קפנדריא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the אגדה and goes back to the הלכה of the משנה. It quotes an unfamiliar word and asks for its meaning, setting up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that even a ruined בית כנסת keeps some of its holiness, so some uses are not allowed. To know what is forbidden, we first need to understand the word קפנדריא.

keyTerms.meaning: We may not make it into

phrases.english: We may not make it a kappendarya.
What is a 'kappendarya'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to explaining the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word קפנדריא.

steps.title: רבא: the word means what it sounds like
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that קפנדריא means what its name suggests.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A קפנדריא is as its name says.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a short answer: the word explains itself. The גמרא will ask in the next step what he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not give a definition yet. He hints that the word's sound tells you its meaning, which the next step will spell out.

phrases.english: Rava said: A kappendarya is as its name says.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word's meaning comes from its name.

steps.title: Explaining the name: instead of going around, cut through
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains 'as its name says': it sounds like a person saying 'instead of going around the row of houses, I'll go through this one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'as its name' mean? Like someone who says: 'Instead of going around the houses, I will go in through this one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבא meant and then explains. קפנדריא sounds like מקיפנא אדרי, 'I'd have to go around the houses', meaning a shortcut through a building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read as a shortened form of a whole Aramaic sentence. So the forbidden use is walking through the בית כנסת just to save time getting to the other side. That treats the holy place like a hallway.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of going around the rows of houses
I will go in through this one

phrases.english: What does 'as its name' mean?
Like someone who says:
'Instead of going around the houses,'
'I will go in through this one.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out רבא's brief answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קפנדריא is a shortcut through a building, from 'instead of going around the houses, I'll go through here.'

steps.title: If a path was there first, walking through is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says that if a public path ran through that spot before the בית כנסת was built, people may keep using it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: If there was a path there from the start, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו adds an exception to the rule of קפנדריא. If the public already had a path there before the building, they may still walk through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on shortcuts is about respect for the בית כנסת. But the public's right to an older path came first, and building a בית כנסת cannot take that right away. The rule stays the same; this is only a case where it does not apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the holiness of a בית כנסת does not cancel a public right of way that existed before it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
If there was a path there originally, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אִם הָיָה שְׁבִיל מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ban on קפנדריא that was just defined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using a בית כנסת as a shortcut is permitted if a public path ran there before it was built.

steps.title: Entering for another reason, then leaving through the other side
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rules that a person who did not enter in order to take a shortcut may leave through the other side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Someone who goes into a בית כנסת without planning to use it as a shortcut is allowed to use it as a shortcut on his way out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a lenient rule to the ban on using a בית כנסת as a shortcut. If the person's entry was not for the shortcut, he may exit through the far side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban only covers walking in for the purpose of cutting through. Here the person came in for some other reason. Since the shortcut was not why he entered, leaving through the far door is no disrespect.

keyTerms.meaning: With the intention of; on condition that

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
One who enters with the intention
not to make it a shortcut —
is permitted to make it a shortcut.
phrases.notes: Meaning: he may leave through the exit on the other side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second lenient exception to the קפנדריא ban, alongside רבי אבהו's public-path rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deciding factor is why the person entered. If he did not enter to take a shortcut, he may exit through the other side.

steps.title: Someone who came to pray may leave by a different door
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו, quoting רב הונא, allows a person who entered to pray to leave through another exit, and supports this with a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: Someone who enters a בית כנסת to pray may use it as a shortcut. As the פסוק says: 'When the people of the land come before ה׳ on the festivals, whoever comes in through the north gate to bow down shall go out through the south gate.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another lenient rule. If you came in to pray, you may leave through a different door, and the גמרא brings a פסוק to back this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes people at the בית המקדש entering through one gate and leaving through the opposite gate. This shows that leaving by another door is a respectful practice, not a disrespectful one. Applied to a בית כנסת, exiting the far side after praying is fine and may even be proper.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רב הונא's rule as permission to walk through a בית כנסת for convenience. It applies only to someone who entered in order to pray.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna:
One who enters a synagogue to pray —
is permitted to make it a shortcut,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּבְבֹא עַם הָאָרֶץ לִפְנֵי ה׳ בַּמּוֹעֲדִים
phrases.english: as it says: "And when the people of the land come before the Lord at the festivals,
whoever comes by way of the north gate to bow down
shall go out by way of the south gate."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another lenient case for קפנדריא, this time with a source from a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who entered to pray may leave through a different exit. This is modeled on how people left the בית המקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practice of leaving a בית כנסת by a different door than the one you came in through.

steps.title: Grass growing in a ruined בית כנסת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if grass grows in a ruined בית כנסת, one should not pick it, because of עגמת נפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If grass grew in it, one should not pick it, because of the sadness it causes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up a question that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the grass in place makes people feel the pain of a destroyed בית כנסת. That pain pushes them to rebuild it. So the משנה forbids picking the grass.

phrases.english: If grass sprang up in it —
phrases.notes: Referring to a ruined בית כנסת

phrases.english: one should not pick it, because of the anguish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next rule in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grass that grows in a ruined בית כנסת should not be picked, because of עגמת נפש.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to allow picking
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids picking the grass to feed animals but allows picking it and leaving it there, which seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: One may not pick it and feed it to animals, but one may pick it and leave it there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא. The ברייתא appears to allow picking the grass in some cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to forbid all picking. The ברייתא allows picking as long as you do not take the grass for your own use. The two sources look like they disagree.

phrases.english: But it is taught: one may not pick and feed,
but one may pick and leave it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's seemingly total ban on picking grass
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows picking the grass and leaving it, so picking cannot be completely forbidden.

steps.title: The משנה only forbids picking to feed animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה was also speaking only about picking the grass to feed animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we learned the משנה too, we learned it as 'picking and feeding.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by narrowing what the משנה forbids. The משנה, like the ברייתא, is only talking about picking for use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the grass as animal feed is like making personal use of the בית כנסת. Picking it and leaving it there is not forbidden. Read this way, the משנה and the ברייתא agree.
steps.whatToRemember: In a ruined בית כנסת, picking the grass to feed animals is forbidden. Picking it and leaving it there is allowed.

phrases.english: When we learned our mishnah as well —
we learned it as 'picking and feeding.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה forbids only picking the grass to feed animals.

steps.title: How to treat a בית הקברות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists what may not be done in a בית הקברות and explains it as כבוד מתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: In a בית הקברות, one may not act lightheartedly. One may not graze animals there, run a water channel through it, or gather grass there. If one did gather grass, it is burned on the spot. This is out of respect for the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא about respect for a בית הקברות, similar to the respect owed a בית כנסת. The reason at the end will be analyzed in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives several prohibitions, then says what to do if grass was gathered, then gives one reason: כבוד מתים. It is unclear which clause that reason explains, and that sets up the next question.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: cemeteries,
one may not behave in them with frivolity.
One may not graze an animal in them,
and one may not run a water channel through them,
and one may not gather grass in them.
And if one gathered — he burns them on the spot,
out of respect for the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא about respect for another holy place, a בית הקברות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית הקברות must not be treated lightly or used for personal benefit. Grass gathered there is burned on the spot.

steps.title: Which clause does 'respect for the dead' explain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of the ברייתא the reason כבוד מתים refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: To which part does this reason go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא. This opens a short back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason comes at the very end, so it could explain the last clause or the first one. The גמרא wants to pin down which.

keyTerms.meaning: To which one? (Which clause does it refer to?)

phrases.english: To which [clause does it refer]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the structure of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which clause of the ברייתא the reason כבוד מתים explains

steps.title: It cannot go on the last clause
steps.stepSummary: The reason cannot explain burning the grass, because burning it quietly on the spot shows no respect to the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it goes on the last clause: since he burns the grass right there, what respect for the dead is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility, that the reason explains the last clause, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning the grass on the spot is done quietly, and no one sees it. Such a private act does not publicly honor the dead. So כבוד מתים cannot be the reason for burning.

keyTerms.meaning: In their place, on the spot

phrases.english: If you say it refers to the last clause —
since he burns them on the spot,
what respect for the dead is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Reading כבוד מתים as the reason for the last clause
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Burning grass privately on the spot does not visibly honor the dead.

steps.title: It goes on the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The reason כבוד מתים explains the first clause, the ban on קלות ראש in a בית הקברות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it goes on the first clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that 'respect for the dead' explains the opening rule. That rule is the ban on frivolous behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Acting lightheartedly near the dead is a direct insult to them. That makes כבוד מתים a natural reason for that clause. The burning rule must rest on some other reason.
steps.whatToRemember: In the ברייתא, the reason כבוד מתים explains the ban on קלות ראש in a בית הקברות, not the rule about burning the grass.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to the first clause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining option after the first one was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כבוד מתים explains the first clause, the ban on קלות ראש.

steps.title: When the Shekalim portion is read
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if ראש חודש אדר falls on שבת, פרשת שקלים is read that day. If it falls during the week, the reading is moved to the שבת before, and the next שבת has no special reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: When ראש חודש אדר falls on שבת, we read פרשת שקלים. If it falls during the week, we move the reading earlier, to the שבת before, and we skip the special readings on the next שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us when to read פרשת שקלים, the first of the four special readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The anchor date is ראש חודש אדר. If it is on שבת, we read שקלים that day. If it is midweek, we never read late, so we read on the שבת before. Then the first שבת of אדר gets no special reading. That is the 'break' (מפסיקין).

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah section about the half-שקל donation (שמות ל׳), read around ראש חודש אדר
The first day of the month of אדר
During the week (not on שבת itself)
We pause or skip; here, no special reading that שבת

steps.confusionAlert: בְּתוֹךְ הַשַּׁבָּת does NOT mean 'on שבת'. Here 'שבת' means the week, so it means 'in the middle of the week.' Also, מַפְסִיקִין here means skipping the special reading for one שבת. In the last line of the משנה, the same word means interrupting the regular weekly reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical rule that שבת שקלים is the שבת on or before ראש חודש אדר.

phrases.english: MISHNAH

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת
phrases.english: The New Moon of Adar that happens to fall on Shabbat
they read the portion of Shekalim
If it happens to fall in the middle of the week
they move it earlier, to the past (previous) Shabbat
and they pause (no special reading) on the next Shabbat
phrases.notes: The first שבת of אדר then has no special portion.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, after the earlier discussion of בית הקברות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פרשת שקלים is read on ראש חודש אדר if it falls on שבת. Otherwise it is read on the שבת before, and the following שבת is skipped.

steps.title: The order of the remaining special readings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the next special readings: זכור on the second, פרה אדומה on the third, החודש הזה לכם on the fourth. On the fifth, the regular order returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the second special שבת we read 'זכור'. On the third, פרה אדומה. On the fourth, 'החודש הזה לכם'. On the fifth, we go back to the regular order.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the schedule. It lists the other three special readings in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Second, third, fourth' counts the special-reading שבתות, not simply calendar weeks, since skipped שבתות are not counted. זכור (about עמלק) comes before פורים. פרה (purity) and החודש (the קרבן פסח) prepare us for ניסן and פסח. After these four, the weekly פרשה cycle continues.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion about remembering what עמלק did (דברים כ״ה)
The red heifer portion, about purifying from טומאת מת (במדבר י״ט)
The portion about the month of ניסן and the קרבן פסח (שמות י״ב)
They return to the regular order

steps.whatToRemember: The four special portions, in order: שקלים, זכור, פרה, החודש. Then the regular weekly reading resumes.

phrases.english: On the second: 'Remember'
On the third: the Red Heifer
On the fourth: 'This month shall be for you'
On the fifth they return to their regular order

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the schedule that began with שקלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order is זכור, then פרה, then החודש. Afterward the regular reading resumes.

steps.title: Special days that interrupt the regular reading
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists days on which the regular weekly reading is set aside for a special reading: ראשי חדשים, חנוכה, פורים, fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all of these we interrupt the regular order: on ראשי חדשים, on חנוכה and פורים, on fast days and מעמדות, and on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a general list of days that get their own special Torah reading instead of the regular one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These days have a reading that fits the day's theme, and it replaces or interrupts the normal sequence. This shows the four special שבתות are part of a wider rule: a special day gets its own reading.

keyTerms.meaning: For all of these, we interrupt the regular reading
Groups of regular Jews who stood in for the people during the Temple service of their week, and read from the Torah

phrases.english: For all of them they interrupt (the regular order)
on New Moons, on Hanukkah and on Purim
on fast days and on the non-priestly watches
and on Yom Kippur

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the topic from the four special שבתות to all special days that interrupt the regular order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On these special days, the regular reading order is interrupted for a reading that fits the day.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the Shekalim announcement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a משנה in מסכת שקלים: on the first of אדר, the public is told about the coming half-שקל collection.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: On the first of אדר, they make an announcement about the שקלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a related משנה from מסכת שקלים. This is a setup line: the גמרא is preparing to ask a question about it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The half-שקל paid for the public קרבנות of the new year, which began in ניסן. So people were reminded a month earlier, on ראש חודש אדר. This explains why our משנה connects פרשת שקלים to ראש חודש אדר. On the next amud, the גמרא will ask for the source of this announcement.

keyTerms.meaning: The half-שקל coins everyone gave for the public offerings

phrases.english: GEMARA
We learned there (in a mishna in Shekalim)
On the first of Adar they announce concerning the shekels

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the משנה by bringing in a related משנה about the שקלים announcement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The public announcement about the half-שקל is made on the first of אדר.
